Apple___Apple_scab.label: Apple___Apple_scab
symptoms: Olive-green to velvety dark brown lesions on upper leaf surfaces
Crinkled, puckered, or distorted leaf margins
Premature defoliation reducing photosynthetic capacity
suggested_actions: Rake and destroy fallen overwintering leaves beneath tree canopy
Prune canopy branches to improve sunlight penetration and air circulation
Avoid overhead misting or late evening irrigation
cultural_remedies: Apply urea (5%) spray to fallen leaves in autumn to accelerate fungal decomposition
Maintain wide tree spacing to allow leaves to dry within 4 hours after dew or rainfall
Mulch orchard floor with organic straw to suppress soil spore splash
prevention: Plant scab-resistant cultivars (e.g., Liberty, Prima, GoldRush)
Perform early spring dormant copper spray before green tip stage
Monitor tree phenology and orchard humidity after continuous rain
cure: Foliar bio-agent: Bacillus subtilis or potassium bicarbonate spray
Standard IPM fungicide: Captan 50 WP (2.5 g/L) or Difenoconazole 25 EC (0.5 mL/L) at early pink bud stage
Ensure adherence to label pre-harvest intervals (PHI)
Apple___Apple_scab.consult_threshold: Consult district horticultural officer if leaf lesions exceed 15% of spur leaves.

Apple___Black_rot.label: Apple___Black_rot
symptoms: Frog-eye leaf spots with purple margins and tan/brown centers
Small black pycnidia (fruiting bodies) visible within mature spots
Twig cankers and mummified rotting fruit hanging on branches
suggested_actions: Prune out dead wood, fire blight strikes, and cankered twigs 15cm below infection
Remove all mummified fruit from trees and ground immediately
Disinfect pruning shears with 70% isopropyl alcohol between cuts
cultural_remedies: Paint winter pruning wounds with protective organic wound sealant
Maintain tree vigor through balanced soil potassium and phosphorus
Keep orchard borders clear of wild brush and dead brambles
prevention: Avoid mechanical damage to bark and trunks during tillage
Apply dormant lime sulfur spray before bud burst
Inspect trees bi-weekly from petal fall through mid-summer
cure: Protective foliar application of Mancozeb 75 WP or Captan 50 WP
Apply Thiophanate-methyl if canker exudation is detected in early spring
Apple___Black_rot.consult_threshold: Contact local extension officer if limb cankers encircle main scaffold branches.

Apple___Cedar_apple_rust.label: Apple___Cedar_apple_rust
symptoms: Bright orange-yellow circular spots on upper leaf surfaces
Raised tube-like aecia structures forming on the underside of leaves
Early leaf drop leading to reduced fruit sizing
suggested_actions: Identify and remove alternate hosts (Eastern Red Cedar/Juniper trees) within 500m where possible
Rake and remove infected foliage from orchard rows
Inspect nearby cedar windbreaks for gelatinous orange rust galls
cultural_remedies: Prune out galls from nearby ornamental junipers during dry winter months
Plant resistant apple varieties like Redfree, Liberty, and Enterprise
Promote tree vigor with organic foliar seaweed extracts
prevention: Avoid planting susceptible cultivars in close proximity to cedar forests
Apply preventative sulfur or copper sprays before springtime rain events
cure: Apply Myclobutanil (Systhane) or Tebuconazole fungicide at tight cluster stage
Bio-fungicide: Neem oil extract (0.5%) as protective barrier on emerging foliage
Apple___Cedar_apple_rust.consult_threshold: Report widespread defoliation in young saplings to your local agriculture officer.

Apple___healthy.label: Apple___healthy
symptoms: Leaves display rich green color with intact cuticle and smooth margins
Absence of chlorotic spots, rust pustules, or powdery mycelium
Normal spur development and leaf vein turgidity
suggested_actions: Continue routine orchard sanitation and regulated irrigation
Maintain balanced N-P-K fertilization based on annual soil tests
Conduct weekly pest scouting for early spider mite or aphid populations
cultural_remedies: Apply composted farmyard manure around the drip line in early spring
Maintain sod or clover ground cover to preserve soil microbial life
prevention: Sterilize all pruning equipment seasonally
Install pheromone traps for codling moth monitoring
cure: No chemical intervention required. Preserve beneficial predators (ladybugs, lacewings).
Apple___healthy.consult_threshold: Consult horticultural officer only if uncharacteristic leaf yellowing appears.

Blueberry___healthy.label: Blueberry___healthy
symptoms: Firm, glossy elliptical leaves with bright green pigmentation
No signs of anthracnose leaf spot, mummy berry, or stem blight
Vigorous shoot growth and strong terminal buds
suggested_actions: Maintain acidic soil pH (between 4.5 and 5.2) with sulfur applications
Provide consistent soil moisture through drip irrigation
Replenish pine bark or sawdust mulch layer (5-8 cm depth)
cultural_remedies: Use organic pine needle mulch to regulate soil temperature and acidity
Avoid excess nitrogen fertilizers that provoke succulent, susceptible shoots
prevention: Ensure excellent soil drainage; avoid waterlogged root zones
Prune old canes (over 5 years) annually to stimulate new basal growth
cure: No treatment needed. Foliage is in healthy physiological condition.
Blueberry___healthy.consult_threshold: Test soil and leaf tissue pH annually with local agricultural university lab.

Cherry_(including_sour)___Powdery_mildew.label: Cherry_(including_sour)___Powdery_mildew
symptoms: White circular powdery patches of fungal mycelium on underside of leaves
Leaves curl upward, cup, and become brittle or distorted
Infected terminal shoots become stunted and winter-tender
suggested_actions: Prune infected terminal shoots and water sprouts that harbor overwintering mycelium
Increase canopy air movement through selective branch thinning
Irrigate via micro-drip rather than overhead sprinklers
cultural_remedies: Foliar spray of 10% cow milk or whey solution under sunny conditions
Apply horticultural mineral oil (1%) to smother active conidial spores
Avoid heavy late-summer nitrogen applications
prevention: Select resistant sour cherry varieties where available
Monitor young expanding leaves starting at petal fall
Maintain weed-free tree basins
cure: Bio-pesticide: Ampelomyces quisqualis or Bacillus subtilis formulation
Approved fungicide: Wettable sulfur (3 g/L) or Trifloxystrobin at first sign of powdery patches
Cherry_(including_sour)___Powdery_mildew.consult_threshold: Consult horticulture specialist if powdery mildew spreads to green fruit surfaces.

Cherry_(including_sour)___healthy.label: Cherry_(including_sour)___healthy
symptoms: Smooth, lustrous, dark green ovate leaves
No shot-hole perforations, powdery coating, or leaf spot lesions
Healthy internode spacing and robust terminal bud set
suggested_actions: Maintain uniform drip irrigation schedule during fruit swell
Apply balanced organic compost to maintain root zone organic matter
Scout for cherry fruit fly and aphids on young shoot tips
cultural_remedies: Apply straw mulch to prevent soil moisture fluctuation
Paint lower trunks with white latex wash to prevent winter sunscald
prevention: Prune during dry summer weather to prevent silver leaf fungal entry
Apply preventative copper wash at late autumn leaf drop
cure: No intervention required. Plant condition is optimal.
Cherry_(including_sour)___healthy.consult_threshold: Consult expert if sudden premature yellow leaf drop occurs.

Corn_(maize)___Cercospora_leaf_spot Gray.label: Corn_(maize)___Cercospora_leaf_spot Gray_leaf_spot
symptoms: Narrow, rectangular tan or gray lesions restricted by leaf veins
Lesions expand longitudinally (2-5 cm) giving a striped appearance
Premature blighting of canopy leading to lodging and stalk rot
suggested_actions: Bury or chop crop residue after harvest to accelerate debris breakdown
Rotate out of corn for 1-2 seasons with pulses, soybeans, or groundnuts
Ensure balanced fertilization with adequate potassium
cultural_remedies: Avoid continuous corn mono-cropping in high humidity valleys
Adopt conservation tillage only with resistant hybrid selection
Reduce plant density slightly to promote lower-canopy aeration
prevention: Plant gray leaf spot resistant hybrid seed (e.g., Pioneer/DeKalb resistant lines)
Treat seeds with Thiram + Carbendazim before sowing
cure: Foliar spray of Azoxystrobin (18.2%) + Difenoconazole (11.4%) SC at 1 mL/L
Apply Pyraclostrobin at tassel (VT) to silking (R1) if lesions reach third leaf below ear leaf
Corn_(maize)___Cercospora_leaf_spot Gray.consult_threshold: Consult Agricultural Extension Officer if lesions appear on ear leaves before tasseling.

Corn_(maize)___Common_rust_.label: Corn_(maize)___Common_rust_
symptoms: Small, oval to elongate cinnamon-brown pustules on both leaf surfaces
Pustules rupture the epidermis releasing powdery brownish-red urediniospores
Chlorosis and necrosis around pustule clusters on older leaves
suggested_actions: Sow early in the planting window to escape peak airborne spore migration
Scout whorl and middle leaves weekly during cool (16-25°C), humid weather
Destroy volunteer corn plants and alternate Oxalis weed hosts
cultural_remedies: Practice balanced nitrogen application; split doses to avoid lush growth
Ensure field borders are clear of weeds
prevention: Cultivate rust-resistant corn hybrids with Rp resistance genes
Maintain recommended plant spacing (60 x 20 cm) for canopy ventilation
cure: Spray Mancozeb 75 WP (2.5 g/L) or Propiconazole 25 EC (1 mL/L) at first sign of pustules
Bio-agent: Trichoderma harzianum soil and foliar application
Corn_(maize)___Common_rust_.consult_threshold: Alert Mandal Agricultural Officer if rust severity exceeds 15% on upper leaves.

Corn_(maize)___Northern_Leaf_Blight.label: Corn_(maize)___Northern_Leaf_Blight
symptoms: Large, elliptical or cigar-shaped grayish-green to tan lesions (3-15 cm long)
Dark, olive-colored fungal spores visible inside lesions in damp conditions
Lesions coalesce, causing extensive blighting and premature leaf death
suggested_actions: Deep plow crop residues after harvest to bury fungal conidia
Implement a minimum 2-year rotation with non-host crops (soybean, cotton)
Scout lower leaves first, especially after heavy rains with temperatures between 18-27°C
cultural_remedies: Avoid overhead irrigation that extends canopy wetness duration
Maintain adequate potash levels in soil to build leaf tissue resilience
prevention: Sow certified NCLB-resistant hybrids with Ht gene resistance
Seed treatment with metalaxyl or thiram
cure: Foliar spray of Azoxystrobin + Tebuconazole (1 mL/L) or Mancozeb 75 WP (2.5 g/L)
Repeat at 14-day intervals if weather remains overcast and humid
Corn_(maize)___Northern_Leaf_Blight.consult_threshold: Contact Rythu Vedika if lesions reach the ear leaf prior to kernel filling.

Corn_(maize)___healthy.label: Corn_(maize)___healthy
symptoms: Broad, arching leaves with uniform deep green coloration
Intact leaf margins free of necrotic lesions, pustules, or striping
Stout, sturdy stalks with strong prop roots and vigorous silking
suggested_actions: Maintain timely irrigation schedule (critical at tasseling and silking stages)
Apply recommended top-dressing of urea at knee-high and pretasseling phases
Install pheromone traps for Fall Armyworm (Spodoptera frugiperda) monitoring
cultural_remedies: Intercrop with pulses (cowpea, green gram) to promote natural pest enemies
Incorporate neem cake into soil during field preparation
prevention: Maintain proper drainage to prevent waterlogging during monsoon showers
Use certified seeds treated with biological inoculants
cure: No chemical spray required. Continue routine agronomic management.
Corn_(maize)___healthy.consult_threshold: Consult MAO if nutrient deficiencies (such as V-shaped nitrogen yellowing) arise.

Grape___Black_rot.label: Grape___Black_rot
symptoms: Small reddish-brown circular spots on leaves with dark borders
Tiny black pycnidia pimples forming a ring inside the leaf spots
Infected berries shrivel into hard, black, wrinkled mummies
suggested_actions: Prune and destroy all mummified berries hanging on canes or on ground
Prune grapevines during dormancy to open canopy to airflow and sunlight
Cultivate beneath trellis rows to bury infected leaf debris
cultural_remedies: Train vines on high trellis systems to improve air movement
Remove sucker shoots near base that serve as initial infection ladders
prevention: Plant less susceptible cultivars or rootstocks
Apply early spring copper spray before bud swell
cure: Spray Myclobutanil 10 WP (0.5 g/L) or Mancozeb 75 WP (2 g/L) from bud break through veraison
Bio-agent: Spray Trichoderma harzianum post-pruning
Grape___Black_rot.consult_threshold: Contact Viticulture Officer if black rot appears on young fruit clusters before pea-size stage.

Grape___Esca_(Black_Measles).label: Grape___Esca_(Black_Measles)
symptoms: 'Tiger-stripe' chlorotic and necrotic patterns between leaf veins
Small, dark, measles-like spots on berry skins
Sudden vine apoplexy (wilting and collapse) during hot dry spells
suggested_actions: Mark infected vines in summer; prune them last to avoid spreading wood pathogens
Disinfect pruning shears with ethanol or bleach solution between vines
Remove and incinerate severely declining or dead grapevines
cultural_remedies: Apply wound sealants or Trichoderma paste to pruning cuts over 2 cm diameter
Avoid heavy mechanical pruning during wet or rainy conditions
Renew trunks using healthy basal suckers where possible
prevention: Purchase certified pathogen-free nursery planting stock
Delay annual pruning until late winter when wound healing is faster
cure: No chemical cure exists for internal wood decay.
Trunk renewal and wound protectant fungicides (Tebuconazole paste) slow disease progression.
Grape___Esca_(Black_Measles).consult_threshold: Immediate consultation with Grape Research Station or Horticultural Officer required.

Grape___Leaf_blight_(Isariopsis_Leaf_Spo.label: Grape___Leaf_blight_(Isariopsis_Leaf_Spot)
symptoms: Irregular reddish-brown lesions with distinct dark borders on mature leaves
Sooty or olive-brown fungal growth on lesion undersides in humid air
Leaves turn chlorotic, curl, and suffer early post-harvest defoliation
suggested_actions: Collect and destroy infected autumn leaves after pruning
Thin foliage canopy around fruit zones to facilitate rapid leaf drying
Avoid overhead irrigation that wets the grapevine foliage
cultural_remedies: Apply balanced potassium fertilizers to prevent late-season foliage weakness
Maintain clean vineyard floor free of wild Vitis weeds
prevention: Apply protective post-harvest copper oxychloride spray
Ensure wide row orientation parallel to prevailing winds
cure: Spray Carbendazim 50 WP (1 g/L) or Copper Oxychloride 50 WP (2.5 g/L)
Bio-agent: Foliar spray of Pseudomonas fluorescens (5 g/L)
Grape___Leaf_blight_(Isariopsis_Leaf_Spo.consult_threshold: Consult horticultural officer if premature defoliation occurs before fruit ripening.

Grape___healthy.label: Grape___healthy
symptoms: Vibrant green palmately-lobed leaves with crisp, intact margins
No fungal spotting, powdery coating, or vascular discoloration
Vigorous tendril growth and balanced cluster-to-leaf ratio
suggested_actions: Maintain regulated deficit irrigation (RDI) for optimal berry quality
Perform shoot positioning and summer canopy trimming as per standard practice
Scout for thrips, mealybugs, and downy mildew after intermittent rains
cultural_remedies: Apply organic compost or vermicompost along vine rows
Maintain grass cover crops between vine rows to build soil carbon
prevention: Install insect yellow sticky traps for monitoring
Ensure correct trellising tension and canopy ventilation
cure: No treatment needed. Vineyard canopy is in excellent health.
Grape___healthy.consult_threshold: Consult viticulturist for petiole nutrient analysis at bloom stage.

Orange___Haunglongbing_(Citrus_greening).label: Orange___Haunglongbing_(Citrus_greening)
symptoms: Asymmetric blotchy mottle (yellowing) crossing leaf veins
Hard, corky, raised leaf veins with zinc/iron deficiency imitation
Lopsided, small, bitter fruit that stays green at the bottom (stylar end)
suggested_actions: Actively control vector: Asian Citrus Psyllid (Diaphorina citri)
Remove and destroy confirmed symptomatic trees to protect healthy grove
Prune back symptomatic shoots if disease is limited to single limb in early detection
cultural_remedies: Apply foliar nutritional sprays (Zinc, Manganese, Iron, Magnesium) to alleviate phloem starvation
Erect windbreaks around the citrus orchard to impede psyllid flight vectors
prevention: Use only certified disease-free budwood from certified screenhouses
Scout new flushes bi-weekly for citrus psyllid nymphs
cure: No chemical cure exists for infected trees.
Vector control: Spray Imidacloprid 17.8 SL (0.5 mL/L) or Thiamethoxam 25 WG (0.3 g/L) on new flushes.
Organic vector control: Neem oil (1%) or horticultural mineral oil.
Orange___Haunglongbing_(Citrus_greening).consult_threshold: Mandatory reporting to District Agricultural / Horticultural Officer and ICAR-CCRI.

Peach___Bacterial_spot.label: Peach___Bacterial_spot
symptoms: Angular, water-soaked dark purple to black leaf spots near margins
Leaf spots drop out, producing a characteristic 'shot-hole' effect
Severe leaf yellowing and early defoliation; gummy pitted lesions on fruit
suggested_actions: Avoid high-nitrogen fertilizer applications that stimulate excessive succulent growth
Prune cankered twigs during dry winter dormancy
Install orchard windbreaks to minimize wind-driven sand abrasion
cultural_remedies: Maintain soil calcium and potassium levels to reinforce leaf epidermal walls
Avoid working in orchards when trees are wet from dew or rain
prevention: Plant resistant peach cultivars (e.g., Clayton, Candor, Biscoe)
Apply dormant copper sprays before bud swell in early spring
cure: Apply Copper hydroxide (Kocide) at low rates during early season flushes
Bactericide: Oxytetracycline (Mycoshield) sprays during post-bloom periods under high disease pressure
Peach___Bacterial_spot.consult_threshold: Consult horticultural officer if bacterial shot-holes cause >20% defoliation.

Peach___healthy.label: Peach___healthy
symptoms: Long, lanceolate, glossy green leaves with serrated margins
Absence of bacterial shot-holes, leaf curl distortion, or rust spots
Healthy terminal shoot extension and vigorous shoot wood
suggested_actions: Maintain drip irrigation schedule matching tree evapotranspiration demand
Perform summer thinning to maintain an open-center vase canopy structure
Monitor for oriental fruit moth and peach tree borer
cultural_remedies: Apply organic compost around the drip circle in late autumn
Keep tree trunks painted with white protective wash
prevention: Sterilize pruning tools between blocks
Ensure good orchard floor weed management
cure: No chemical intervention needed. Tree foliage is healthy.
Peach___healthy.consult_threshold: Consult fruit extension specialist if leaves begin curling or blistering.

Pepper,_bell___Bacterial_spot.label: Pepper,_bell___Bacterial_spot
symptoms: Small, circular to irregular water-soaked spots on leaves
Spots turn dark brown or black with a pale halo on undersides
Leaves turn chlorotic and drop prematurely, exposing fruit to sunscald
suggested_actions: Remove and bury infected lower leaves during dry morning hours
Avoid overhead sprinkler irrigation; switch entirely to drip lines
Do not cultivate or handle pepper plants while dew is on the leaves
cultural_remedies: Practice 2-3 year crop rotation with non-solanaceous crops (maize, beans, sorghum)
Sterilize stakes, seed trays, and greenhouse tools with 10% bleach solution
Mulch beds with silver reflective or black plastic mulch
prevention: Sow certified hot-water treated or disease-free seeds
Plant resistant pepper hybrids (carrying Bs2 or Bs3 resistance genes)
cure: Foliar spray of Copper Hydroxide (2 g/L) + Streptocycline (100 ppm / 1 g in 10 L water)
Bio-control: Foliar application of Bacillus amyloliquefaciens
Pepper,_bell___Bacterial_spot.consult_threshold: Contact Mandal Agricultural Officer if spotting spreads across >30% of beds.

Pepper,_bell___healthy.label: Pepper,_bell___healthy
symptoms: Deep green, smooth, ovate leaves with prominent veins
No necrotic lesions, mosaics, leaf curling, or bacterial water-soaking
Robust flowering and vigorous fruit set
suggested_actions: Maintain consistent soil moisture to prevent blossom-end rot
Apply balanced fertilizer with calcium and magnesium supplements
Scout for thrips and mites on undersides of new leaves
cultural_remedies: Apply organic neem cake in root zone to prevent soil nematodes
Maintain uniform drip fertigation schedule
prevention: Install blue and yellow sticky traps for early thrips detection
Ensure well-drained, raised planting beds
cure: No chemical intervention required. Foliage is in prime health.
Pepper,_bell___healthy.consult_threshold: Consult horticultural specialist if upward leaf curling occurs.

Potato___Early_blight.label: Potato___Early_blight
symptoms: Circular brown lesions with characteristic concentric rings ('target-board' pattern)
Yellow chlorotic halo surrounding older leaf spots
Lesions expand, dry out, and cause premature lower canopy defoliation
suggested_actions: Prune off and safely dispose of severely infected lower leaves
Maintain adequate nitrogen and potassium to avoid premature plant senescence
Avoid overhead irrigation; keep foliage dry especially toward evening
cultural_remedies: Practice minimum 3-year crop rotation without potatoes, tomatoes, or eggplants
Hill up rows properly to protect developing tubers from fungal spore rain
Mulch soil surface with clean straw to minimize rain splash
prevention: Plant certified disease-free, vigorous seed tubers (e.g., Kufri Jyoti)
Treat seed tubers with Trichoderma viride (10 g/kg) before planting
cure: Spray Chlorothalonil 75 WP (2 g/L) or Mancozeb 75 WP (2.5 g/L) at first symptom
Systemic option: Difenoconazole 25 EC (0.5 mL/L) or Azoxystrobin (1 mL/L)
Potato___Early_blight.consult_threshold: Consult Agricultural Officer if lesions cover more than 15% of middle canopy foliage.

Potato___Late_blight.label: Potato___Late_blight
symptoms: Large, irregular, water-soaked pale to dark lesions starting at leaf margins and tips
White velvety mildew growth on leaf undersides under cool, moist conditions (>90% RH)
Rapid stem collapse, foul rotting odor, and tuber rot turning brown and dry
suggested_actions: Immediately destroy and bury all infected foliage away from the field
Cease overhead irrigation immediately; drain excess standing field water
De-haulm (cut and remove stems) 10-14 days before harvest if late blight is present
cultural_remedies: Deep soil hilling (covering tubers with at least 10 cm soil) prevents tuber infection
Erect high raised ridges to prevent waterlogging around root zone
Never leave potato cull piles near fields; destroy them completely
prevention: Plant certified late blight resistant cultivars (e.g., Kufri Girdhari, Kufri Himalini)
Apply prophylactic contact fungicide (Mancozeb 75 WP @ 2.5 g/L) before rainy spells
cure: Systemic curatives: Cymoxanil (8%) + Mancozeb (64%) WP @ 2.5 g/L, or Metalaxyl-M + Mancozeb @ 2.5 g/L
Alternative: Dimethomorph 50 WP (1 g/L) combined with a contact fungicide
Potato___Late_blight.consult_threshold: Emergency: Inform Mandal Agricultural Officer (MAO) immediately if late blight is detected.

Potato___healthy.label: Potato___healthy
symptoms: Lush, compound dark green leaves with uniform surface texture
No water-soaked spots, target rings, or white underside mycelium
Erect, vigorous haulms and active stolon formation
suggested_actions: Maintain uniform soil moisture at 65-75% field capacity during tuber bulking
Conduct earthen hilling-up at 30-35 days after planting
Scout for aphid vectors (Myzus persicae) to prevent viral degeneration
cultural_remedies: Incorporate neem cake (250 kg/ha) during soil bed preparation
Ensure proper drainage channels between crop furrows
prevention: Use only certified seed tubers from recognized government seed agencies
Install yellow water pan traps for aphid vector monitoring
cure: No chemical sprays needed. Maintain regular scouting.
Potato___healthy.consult_threshold: Consult extension officer if haulm growth appears stunted or mottled.

Raspberry___healthy.label: Raspberry___healthy
symptoms: Clean, pinnate serrated leaves with rich green upper surfaces
No cane blight lesions, spur blight spotting, or powdery mildew
Strong primocane and floricane vegetative development
suggested_actions: Trellis canes properly to allow sunlight and airflow throughout canopy
Prune spent floricanes immediately after fruiting completes
Maintain soil moisture using drip irrigation beneath woodchip mulch
cultural_remedies: Maintain wood chip mulch (8 cm depth) to suppress weed competition
Keep cane rows narrow (under 45 cm wide) for optimal air penetration
prevention: Ensure good soil drainage; avoid poorly drained clay soils
Plant certified virus-indexed raspberry stock
cure: No treatment necessary. Plant is in excellent condition.
Raspberry___healthy.consult_threshold: Consult horticultural specialist if cane lesions or wilt appear.

Soybean___healthy.label: Soybean___healthy
symptoms: Trifoliate leaves exhibiting vibrant, uniform green coloration
Absence of rust pustules, frog-eye leaf spot, or soybean mosaic chlorosis
Abundant active root nodulation with pink interior leghaemoglobin
suggested_actions: Ensure adequate soil moisture during pod development and seed fill
Scout weekly for pod borers, semiloopers, and whiteflies
Maintain weed-free conditions during the critical first 45 days
cultural_remedies: Inoculate seeds with Bradyrhizobium japonicum before sowing
Intercrop with pigeon pea (arhar) or sorghum for biodiversity
prevention: Rotate annually with non-legume crops (maize, wheat)
Use certified high-germination seed
cure: No chemical intervention required. Continue good agronomic management.
Soybean___healthy.consult_threshold: Consult Agriculture Extension Officer if sudden chlorosis appears across fields.

Squash___Powdery_mildew.label: Squash___Powdery_mildew
symptoms: Powdery white fungal spots on upper and lower surfaces of leaves and stems
Spots enlarge rapidly to cover entire leaf with a talcum powder-like film
Leaves turn prematurely yellow, brown, and dry out like parchment, leading to sunscald on fruits
suggested_actions: Remove and compost or bury older, heavily infected bottom leaves
Increase plant spacing to improve sunlight penetration and air movement
Avoid excess nitrogen fertilizer that fuels tender, susceptible foliage
cultural_remedies: Foliar spray of baking soda (sodium bicarbonate, 4 g/L) + horticultural soap as spreader
Spray diluted milk solution (1 part milk to 9 parts water) under full sunlight
Apply neem oil (0.5%) as an organic preventative spray
prevention: Choose powdery mildew tolerant squash varieties
Water with drip tape; keep foliage completely dry during irrigation
cure: Bio-fungicide: Bacillus subtilis or potassium silicate spray
Approved chemical: Wettable sulfur (2.5 g/L) or Azoxystrobin 23 SC (1 mL/L)
Do not apply sulfur when temperatures exceed 32°C to prevent phytotoxicity
Squash___Powdery_mildew.consult_threshold: Contact Horticultural Officer if powdery mildew reaches fruit stems before harvest.

Strawberry___Leaf_scorch.label: Strawberry___Leaf_scorch
symptoms: Numerous small, irregular, purple to dark reddish spots on upper leaf surfaces
Centers of spots remain dark purple (unlike common leaf spot which turns white)
Leaves scorch, curl up along the edges, turn brown, and resemble burnt foliage
suggested_actions: Remove and destroy infected leaves during post-harvest renovation
Ensure plants are not overcrowded in matted rows
Switch to drip irrigation to prevent overhead leaf wetting
cultural_remedies: Mow, rake, and discard infected foliage after harvest is complete
Maintain straw or pine needle mulch beneath fruit clusters to prevent soil contact
Avoid high spring nitrogen which promotes susceptible lush leaves
prevention: Plant certified disease-free strawberry runners
Select resistant cultivars (e.g., Honeoye, Jewel, Allstar)
cure: Apply Copper hydroxide or Captan 50 WP (2 g/L) in early spring as new leaves emerge
Bio-agent: Foliar spray of Trichoderma harzianum
Strawberry___Leaf_scorch.consult_threshold: Consult horticultural extension officer if scorching reduces leaf area by >25%.

Strawberry___healthy.label: Strawberry___healthy
symptoms: Rich emerald green trifoliate leaves with clean, crisp dentate margins
No purple spotting, scorched leaf tips, or grey mold sporulation
Vigorous runner production and well-formed crown development
suggested_actions: Maintain uniform drip irrigation schedule through plastic mulch
Apply balanced water-soluble fertigation with potassium and boron
Scout for two-spotted spider mites and strawberry aphids
cultural_remedies: Maintain clean straw mulch under ripening berries
Keep runner numbers balanced according to row density goals
prevention: Use drip tape placed beneath black or silver polyethylene mulch
Install predatory mites (Phytoseiulus persimilis) for biological mite balance
cure: No chemical intervention needed. Plants are in peak condition.
Strawberry___healthy.consult_threshold: Consult extension specialist if crown rot or wilting occurs.

Tomato___Bacterial_spot.label: Tomato___Bacterial_spot
symptoms: Small, greasy, water-soaked dark brown spots on leaves, stems, and petioles
Spots turn angular, dark brown with a distinct yellow chlorotic halo
Leaves turn brown and drop; scab-like raised blister spots on green fruit
suggested_actions: Prune infected lower foliage during dry afternoon hours
Never work in wet tomato fields; human touch rapidly transfers bacteria
Disinfect pruning shears with 70% isopropyl alcohol between plants
cultural_remedies: Rotate crops for at least 2 years without solanaceous hosts (eggplant, pepper, potato)
Use drip irrigation exclusively; avoid all overhead water splash
Stake and prune plants to improve airflow in the lower canopy
prevention: Plant certified pathogen-free seeds treated with hot water (50°C for 25 min)
Mulch beds with black plastic or straw to suppress soil-to-leaf splashing
cure: Preventative spray: Copper hydroxide (2 g/L) + Mancozeb (2 g/L) tank mix
Bactericide: Streptocycline (100 ppm) applied at early vegetative stages
Bio-control: Bacillus subtilis or bacteriophage products
Tomato___Bacterial_spot.consult_threshold: Contact local Rythu Vedika if bacterial spotting spreads to fruit trusses.

Tomato___Early_blight.label: Tomato___Early_blight
symptoms: Concentric rings ('target-board' pattern) on older lower leaves
Yellow chlorotic zone surrounding expanding brown lesions
Lower leaves dry up, turn brown, and drop prematurely, causing sunscald
suggested_actions: Prune off the lowest 30 cm of leaves touching the soil or mulch
Stake tomato vines and prune suckers to promote fast drying
Water at the base of plants; do not splash soil onto lower foliage
cultural_remedies: Apply straw or plastic mulch to barrier against soil-borne fungal spores
Practice 3-year crop rotation with non-solanaceous crops (cereals, legumes)
Remove and burn or deep bury all crop residues after final harvest
prevention: Plant tolerant varieties (e.g., Mountain Supreme, Defiant PhR)
Treat seedlings with Trichoderma viride before transplanting
cure: Contact spray: Mancozeb 75 WP (2.5 g/L) or Chlorothalonil 75 WP (2 g/L)
Systemic spray: Difenoconazole 25 EC (0.5 mL/L) or Azoxystrobin (1 mL/L)
Organic: Copper oxychloride + Bacillus subtilis
Tomato___Early_blight.consult_threshold: Consult Agricultural Officer if early blight climbs above the fruit cluster level.

Tomato___Late_blight.label: Tomato___Late_blight
symptoms: Rapidly expanding, pale green to dark water-soaked lesions on leaves and stems
White frost-like fungal sporulation on leaf undersides during cool, humid spells
Entire vine rapidly collapses and rots; fruit develops firm, dark brown greasy rot
suggested_actions: Remove and incinerate or deep-bury infected plants immediately
Halt overhead irrigation immediately; maximize greenhouse/canopy ventilation
Harvest unblemished mature green fruit immediately to prevent field loss
cultural_remedies: Keep canopy well-spaced and staked for rapid moisture evaporation
Destroy any nearby volunteer tomato or potato plants
Never compost late-blight infected plant material
prevention: Plant resistant tomato hybrids (e.g., Mountain Magic, Iron Lady, Legend)
Apply preventative Mancozeb (2.5 g/L) before periods of cool, wet weather
cure: Curative systemic spray: Cymoxanil + Mancozeb (2.5 g/L) or Metalaxyl + Mancozeb (2.5 g/L)
Alternative oomycete fungicide: Dimethomorph 50 WP (1 g/L) or Mandipropamid (0.8 mL/L)
Tomato___Late_blight.consult_threshold: Emergency: Inform local Mandal Agricultural Officer (MAO) immediately upon suspicion.

Tomato___Leaf_Mold.label: Tomato___Leaf_Mold
symptoms: Pale green to yellowish patches on upper leaf surfaces with indistinct borders
Dense, velvety olive-green to brown mold growth on the corresponding underside
Infected leaves wither, turn yellow-brown, and drop prematurely
suggested_actions: Increase greenhouse or polyhouse ventilation immediately to drop relative humidity below 80%
Prune lower suckers and dense interior foliage to allow air to flow through canopy
Space plants adequately (at least 50 cm between plants on rows)
cultural_remedies: Use drip irrigation exclusively; avoid wetting foliage
Wipe down greenhouse structure and stakes with disinfectant between seasons
prevention: Grow leaf mold resistant tomato varieties (carrying Cf-1 to Cf-9 resistance genes)
Ensure heated greenhouses have adequate night-time air circulation
cure: Foliar spray of Copper Oxychloride (2.5 g/L) or Chlorothalonil 75 WP (2 g/L)
Bio-agent: Bio-fungicide spray containing Bacillus amyloliquefaciens
Tomato___Leaf_Mold.consult_threshold: Consult horticultural extension officer if mold severity exceeds 25% of greenhouse canopy.

Tomato___Septoria_leaf_spot.label: Tomato___Septoria_leaf_spot
symptoms: Numerous small, circular spots (1-3 mm) with dark brown borders and grey/tan centers
Tiny black specks (pycnidia) clearly visible in the center of mature spots
Leaves turn completely yellow, wither, dry out, and drop from base upwards
suggested_actions: Prune off infected lower leaves immediately to stop upward fungal climb
Mulch soil around plants with clean straw or plastic to block spore splashing
Stake and tie vines off the ground
cultural_remedies: Practice minimum 2-year crop rotation without solanaceous crops
Deep plow or bury tomato crop debris after harvest
Maintain wide plant spacing (60 x 45 cm) for optimal canopy aeration
prevention: Water at the base of vines; never use overhead sprinklers
Apply protective copper or Mancozeb sprays at transplant establishment
cure: Foliar spray of Chlorothalonil 75 WP (2 g/L) or Mancozeb 75 WP (2.5 g/L)
Systemic curative: Tebuconazole 25.9 EC (1 mL/L) or Difenoconazole (0.5 mL/L)
Tomato___Septoria_leaf_spot.consult_threshold: Consult MAO if defoliation reaches middle canopy during fruit set.

Tomato___Spider_mites Two-spotted_spider.label: Tomato___Spider_mites Two-spotted_spider_mite
symptoms: Fine yellow stippling or white speckling on upper leaf surfaces
Fine silk webbing on undersides of leaves and around growing tips
Leaves turn bronze or yellow, dry up, and plants appear scorched
suggested_actions: Spray plants with a strong jet of water to disrupt mite webs and dislodge adults
Remove and destroy heavily webbed shoots and leaves immediately
Keep farm roads and field perimeters damp to suppress dust (which favors mites)
cultural_remedies: Release predatory mites (Phytoseiulus persimilis or Neoseiulus californicus)
Apply insecticidal soap (20 mL/L) or cold-pressed neem oil (5 mL/L) thoroughly wetting leaf undersides
Avoid broad-spectrum synthetic pyrethroids that kill natural mite predators
prevention: Maintain adequate irrigation; drought-stressed plants are prime mite targets
Monitor undersides of leaves weekly with a 10x hand lens
cure: Targeted miticides: Spiromesifen 22.9 SC (1 mL/L), Fenpyroximate 5 EC (1 mL/L), or Abamectin 1.9 EC (0.5 mL/L)
Rotate miticide modes of action (IRAC groups) to prevent rapid resistance buildup
Tomato___Spider_mites Two-spotted_spider.consult_threshold: Consult entomologist if mite webbing covers growing tips on >10% of plants.

Tomato___Target_Spot.label: Tomato___Target_Spot
symptoms: Small, pinpoint water-soaked spots that enlarge into circular brown lesions
Concentric rings with light brown centers and dark brown margins
Lesions cause severe blighting, premature defoliation, and sunken fruit spots
suggested_actions: Prune suckers and stake plants to improve internal canopy air circulation
Remove and destroy infected leaves from bottom of plant
Avoid overhead irrigation; schedule watering for early morning
cultural_remedies: Practice crop rotation with non-host crops (corn, sorghum)
Remove volunteer weeds (like black nightshade) that harbor Corynespora
Mulch beds to reduce humidity and spore splash
prevention: Maintain optimal potassium and calcium nutrition
Apply preventative copper or chlorothalonil sprays during warm, humid weather
cure: Foliar spray of Azoxystrobin (1 mL/L) or Pyraclostrobin + Boscalid (Pristine)
Contact protectant: Chlorothalonil 75 WP (2 g/L)
Tomato___Target_Spot.consult_threshold: Consult extension officer if target spot appears on green tomato fruits.

Tomato___Tomato_Yellow_Leaf_Curl_Virus.label: Tomato___Tomato_Yellow_Leaf_Curl_Virus
Tomato___Tomato_Yellow_Leaf_Curl_Virus.pathogen: Tomato yellow leaf curl virus (Begomovirus transmitted by Whiteflies)
symptoms: Severe upward curling and cupping of leaf margins
Marked interveinal chlorosis (yellowing) with stunted, bushy foliage
Dramatic reduction in leaf size, flower drop, and near-total loss of fruit yield
suggested_actions: Rogue out and destroy infected viral plants immediately (bag before pulling)
Focus intensively on controlling the insect vector: Whitefly (Bemisia tabaci)
Erect yellow sticky traps (15-20 per acre) across field and borders
cultural_remedies: Install insect-proof 50-mesh netting in nurseries and polyhouses
Use silver reflective mulches that deter whiteflies from landing on young seedlings
Plant border barrier crops (3-4 rows of maize or pearl millet) to intercept incoming whiteflies
prevention: Cultivate TYLCV-resistant tomato hybrids (e.g., US-618, Abhinav, Saaho)
Keep seedling nursery completely insect-screened
cure: No chemical cure exists for viral infection once inside the plant.
Whitefly vector control: Spray Thiamethoxam 25 WG (0.3 g/L) or Diafenthiuron 50 WP (1 g/L)
Organic vector spray: Neem oil 10,000 ppm (2 mL/L) or Beauveria bassiana bio-insecticide
Tomato___Tomato_Yellow_Leaf_Curl_Virus.consult_threshold: Emergency: Report whitefly outbreaks and TYLCV spread immediately to MAO.

Tomato___Tomato_mosaic_virus.label: Tomato___Tomato_mosaic_virus
symptoms: Mottling of leaves with alternating light green and dark green mosaic patterns
Fern-like distortion or 'shoestring' narrowing of leaf blades
Stunting of plants, bronzing or internal browning of fruit walls
suggested_actions: Immediately remove and burn infected plants (handle with disposable gloves)
Workers must wash hands with soapy water or nonfat dry milk (20%) before touching plants
Strictly prohibit smoking or chewing tobacco anywhere near tomato crops
cultural_remedies: Dip tools, stakes, and pruning knives in 10% trisodium phosphate (TSP) or 20% skimmed milk
Sterilize seed-starting trays and nursery soil before sowing
Avoid handling plants unless absolutely necessary
prevention: Plant ToMV-resistant cultivars (e.g., varieties with Tm-2 or Tm-2^2 resistance alleles)
Use certified virus-free seed treated with trisodium phosphate or heat treatment
cure: No chemical treatment or viricide exists for viral infection.
Sanitation and immediate eradication of infected plants are the only effective controls.
Tomato___Tomato_mosaic_virus.consult_threshold: Consult Agriculture Extension Officer for confirmation and seed source trace.

Tomato___healthy.label: Tomato___healthy
symptoms: Dark green compound leaves with crisp margins and healthy glandular hairs
Zero lesions, yellow halos, viral curling, or insect stippling
Vigorous apical growth with abundant balanced truss flowering
suggested_actions: Maintain regular drip irrigation (avoid large fluctuations in moisture to prevent blossom-end rot)
Prune suckers selectively to balance vegetative and reproductive growth
Apply balanced calcium, potassium, and magnesium during fruit set
cultural_remedies: Mulch beds with straw or organic compost to conserve moisture and regulate soil temperature
Intercrop with marigolds to deter root-knot nematodes and attract pollinators
prevention: Stake vines off the ground using strong trellising wires
Install yellow sticky traps for prophylactic insect monitoring
cure: No chemical sprays required. Plant is in prime health.
Tomato___healthy.consult_threshold: Consult MAO if unexpected physiological disorders (like catfacing or blossom-end rot) arise.

rice___blast.label: rice___blast
symptoms: Spindle-shaped or diamond-shaped leaf lesions with grey/white centers and brown borders
Neck rot causing the panicle to collapse and remain empty
Brown or black spots on nodes turning brittle
suggested_actions: Spray Tricyclazole 75 WP or Azoxystrobin fungicide at early symptom detection
Reduce nitrogenous fertilizer application immediately; avoid excess urea
Maintain proper standing water depth in fields to moderate canopy temperature
cultural_remedies: Split nitrogen applications into 3-4 doses paired with potassium
Maintain 2-5 cm standing water layer in paddy basins
Burn or compost infected rice stubble after harvest
prevention: Sow blast-resistant cultivars (e.g., CSR-30, Pusa Basmati 1637, MTU-1010)
Practice seed treatment with Carbendazim (2 g/kg) or Pseudomonas fluorescens (10 g/kg)
cure: Spray Tricyclazole 75 WP (0.6 g/L) or Isoprothiolane 40 EC (1.5 mL/L)
Foliar spray of Pseudomonas fluorescens bio-agent (5 g/L)
rice___blast.consult_threshold: Consult Mandal Agricultural Officer if neck blast appears at heading stage.

wheat___leaf_rust.label: wheat___leaf_rust
symptoms: Small, circular to oval orange-brown pustules scattered randomly on leaf blades
Pustules turn dark brown/black as crop reaches maturity
Chlorosis and premature yellowing of leaf blades reducing grain filling
suggested_actions: Apply Propiconazole or Tebuconazole fungicide sprays promptly
Scout weekly and identify rust clusters early before boot stage
Destroy volunteer wheat plants that harbor spores between seasons
cultural_remedies: Sow within the optimum planting window (Nov 1-15 in North India)
Ensure balanced fertilization with adequate potassium to strengthen cell walls
prevention: Cultivate rust-resistant varieties (e.g., HD-2967, PBW-550, DBW-187)
Seed treatment with Carboxin + Thiram before sowing
cure: Foliar spray of Propiconazole 25 EC (1 mL/L) or Tebuconazole 25.9 EC (1 mL/L)
wheat___leaf_rust.consult_threshold: Alert Agriculture Extension Officer if rust appears before the flag leaf stage.

healthy.label: healthy
symptoms: Clean, dark green foliage with zero lesions
Vibrant leaf texture and intact surface structure
Excellent turgidity and leaf vein integrity
suggested_actions: Maintain current irrigation and weeding schedules
Apply well-rotted farmyard manure or organic compost
Perform regular crop scouting for preventative monitoring
cultural_remedies: Maintain healthy soil biology and crop rotation
Ensure regular supply of micro and macronutrients
prevention: Use pest traps as preventative monitoring
Keep field borders clean of weed reservoirs
cure: No disease cure required. Crop condition is optimal.
healthy.consult_threshold: Consult agricultural expert if uncharacteristic symptoms appear.
